newsitem.title: USA: US 1996 stainless steel imports at 553,221 tons.
newsitem.headline: US 1996 stainless steel imports at 553,221 tons.

text.p: U.S. 1996 imports of stainless steel rose 10 percent to a record 553,221 short tons from 503,501 tons in 1995, an industry trade group said Friday.

The Specialty Steel Industry of North America said that the imports "absorbed most of the healthy U.S. market growth and devastated domestic pricing levels during the year." Imports of stainless steel accounted for 24 percent of the U.S. market, it said.
The group said total 1996 U.S. consumption of stainless steel was 2.3 million tons, a five percent increase from the previous year.

It also said 1996 total specialty steel imports, which include stainless steel, tool and electrical steel, stood at 717,201 tons, up eight percent from the previous year. US 1996 consumption was 2.9 million tons, up five percent from 1995.

The group said it was encouraged by recent developments in its effort to get a Multilateral Speciality Steel Agreement to reduce trade barriers, open foreign markets and restrict government subsidies on steel.

"We are encouraged that U.S. Trade Representative-designate Charlene Barshefsky wrote us recently indicating the U.S. Government's intent to press forward with this effort," the group's chairman, James Will, said.
Barshefsky's letter said the United States would seek "a preliminary agreement with the European Union" and would attempt to "broaden this (agreement) to a wide range of countries," the group said.
